intent: To illustrate that driving alone is the predominant mode of commuting for Americans, highlighting the minimal share of public transportation usage to explain the low reliance on transit.

units.meaning: Drive alone is the largest commuting mode, accounting for 76.3% of commuters.

basis.note: percent of commuting mode share; printed source

accepted_routes: Drive alone accounts for 76.3% of commuting.
About 76% of Americans drive alone to work.
Drive alone is the predominant mode at 76.3%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Drive-alone slice must be clearly the largest and labeled or implied at 76.3% or about 76%.
units.temporal_anchor: Predominant-mode/title clause implied by intent; if narration only has the transit clause, use the chart title or annotation.
units.reviewer_question: Should 76.3% be the headline share for drive alone, or is it enough to show it as the largest slice?

units.meaning: Public transportation accounts for only 5.2% of commuting mode share.

basis.note: percent of commuting mode share; estimated

accepted_routes: Public transportation accounts for 5.2% of commutes.
Public transportation is a small 5.2% slice.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Public-transportation slice must be visibly small and labeled or implied at 5.2% or about 5%.
units.temporal_anchor: Narration clause: 'most Americans don't rely on public transit'.
units.reviewer_question: Should public transportation's 5.2% be shown as an exact label, rounded to about 5%, or only visually small?

units.meaning: Drive alone (76.3%) exceeds all other commuting modes combined, which total 23.7%.
accepted_routes: Drive alone (76.3%) is more than all other modes combined (23.7%).
76.3% drive alone, leaving 23.7% for everything else.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Either a single drive-alone wedge versus combined rest, or an annotation that non-drive-alone modes total 23.7%.
units.temporal_anchor: Predominant-mode clause implied by intent; if narration only has the transit clause, use the chart annotation.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly state that drive alone exceeds all other modes combined?

units.meaning: Public transportation is only about 6.8% as common as driving alone; driving alone is about 14.7 times public transportation.

basis.note: denominator for ratio; also numerator for multiplier

accepted_routes: Public transportation is only about 7% as common as driving alone.
Driving alone is nearly 15 times public transportation.
For every public-transit commuter, about 15 drive alone.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A ratio annotation or side-by-side comparison showing transit is about 1/15 of drive alone, or drive alone is about 14.7 times transit.
units.temporal_anchor: Narration clause: 'low reliance on transit' phrase.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video include a ratio or multiplier between public transit and drive alone, or just separate percentages?

units.meaning: Ranking of modes: drive alone is 1st at 76.3%, carpool 2nd at 8.2%, public transportation 3rd at 5.2% just above work at home at 5.1%, then walk, taxi/motorcycle/other, and bicycle at 1.0%.
accepted_routes: Drive alone > carpool > public transportation > work at home > walk > taxi/motorcycle/other > bicycle.
Public transportation is third at 5.2%, just above work at home at 5.1%, and is not the absolute smallest.
Bicycle is the smallest listed mode at 1.0%.
units.visual_evidence_rule: All slices must be sized or ordered correctly; public transit must not be shown as the smallest slice; bicycle should be the smallest if distinguished.
units.temporal_anchor: Narration clause: 'most Americans don't rely on public transit' or chart legend.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly avoid calling public transportation the smallest mode, given bicycle is 1.0%?

optional_valid: Public transportation (5.2%) and work at home (5.1%) are nearly identical.
Carpool is the second-largest mode at 8.2%.
Bicycle is the smallest listed mode at 1.0%.
Taxi, motorcycle, or other is 1.7% of commuting mode share.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as people drive alone because public transit is 5.2%.
Calling public transportation the absolute smallest mode; bicycle is smaller at 1.0%.
Extrapolating to all trips, non-commute travel, or other years or geographies.
Using a denominator other than commuting mode share, e.g., '5.2% of Americans'.
Implying shares sum to more than 100% or omitting that the table is mode share.
notes: All listed shares sum to 100%; drive alone is printed, others estimated. Avoid treating public transit as the absolute minimum because bicycle is 1.0%.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
